label: recheck-a
tail:
Re-check complete. `research/frontier-14-alpha-a-recheck.md` is written.

**All 18 routed findings are `confirmed` on disk.** No Beta claimed a fix it did not make. Because the scaffolds were committed at 02:31 and the fix dispatches ran 03:38–03:49 uncommitted, `git diff HEAD` *is* the fix pass — so "applied but changed nothing" was mechanically decidable rather than a judgement call.

Three results worth your attention:

**One pushback, partially rejected — D1.** Batch 2's Beta declined to touch the ℂ re-mint, arguing it cannot edit `plan-spec.json`. True but beside the point: batches 1 and 3 both recorded their proposed `requires` in *their own manifests* and said so. Batch 2 didn't, so `stone-weierstrass-general` is the only page in the group where you have no splice-ready option in front of you. Both edges re-verified legal (published, backward, acyclic; all eight published targets exist).

**Two fixes beat what I asked for.** C3: rather than build the real Arzelà–Ascoli case, the Beta checked disk and found it already published (`thm-arzela-ascoli-for-real-ck`, in closure) — so it cites and proves only the genuinely new ℝⁿ clause. A2 likewise: the `sin(iy)=i sinh y` computation is already published verbatim, so it was recorded rather than duplicated.

**Two new findings, R1/R2** (new namespace, nothing renumbered), both inside C1's new Munkres harvest. R1 matters: the harvest maps Munkres §45's equicontinuity to the library's *metric*-domain `def-equicontinuity`, but Munkres states it for a **topological** domain — so the general definition is still recorded BBT-only when Munkres actually backs it. One coverage row converts it to double-treatment.

Gates re-run green non-vacuously (97/74/116 harvested, 73/49/86 scoped, 208 ids with 0 collisions, 20/20 URLs live, all contracts present with 8 real boundary axes). I re-fetched C2's recovered Shapiro URL myself: 3-page `application/pdf`, 53,865 bytes.

**The blocker is yours, not the Betas'.** `step3-decisions.md` still ends at D4, mtime 02:26 — untouched since before my review. I splice-tested both ways: current `requires` → **FAIL, 6 `undeclared-prereq`**; manifest `requires` → **OK, 0 errors**. 305 and 285 are ready now; 307, 277 and 293 need only the §G edges recorded (277's two as a package — the `monoids-groups-and-subgroups` error independently confirms it), and 287 needs a D1 decision either way.

One thing I could not check: the Munkres URL (`djvu.online`) is an HTML scan viewer, not a PDF, so it is unreachable to `pypdf` and to the step-6 faithfulness pass. I verified §45 and Theorem 47.1 against an independent transcription instead; the fifteen §46 rows rest on my own knowledge of the text, which is a weaker check and should be redone at step 6.
